Key Research Thinking Patterns: Robustness Analysis: Investigating the sensitivity of psychometric models (e.g., Graded Response Model (GRM) and 2-Parameter Logistic Model (2PLM)) to violations of assumptions (e.g., normality of latent trait distribution) and exploring the impact of sample size and test length on model performance.

Hierarchical Model Evaluation: Developing and extending frameworks (e.g., dynamic fit index (DFI)) for evaluating the fit of hierarchical and second-order factor models, highlighting the need for customized fit index cutoffs tailored to specific model characteristics.

Methodological Taxonomy: Proposing and refining taxonomies for understanding heterogeneity in research and reporting practices, clarifying areas where more research and methodological guidance are needed, and redefining crucial terms (e.g., researcher degrees of freedom (RDFs) and questionable research practices (QRPs)).

Factor Analysis: Investigating the impact of methodological choices (e.g., determining the number of factors and rotation) on the heterogeneity of Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) results and exploring the relevance of data characteristics in this context.
Summary Description: Patrick Manapat is a researcher specializing in psychometrics, methodology, and statistical analysis. His work focuses on developing and evaluating psychometric models, particularly the Graded Response Model (GRM) and 2-Parameter Logistic Model (2PLM), and exploring their robustness to violations of assumptions. He also investigates the impact of methodological choices on the heterogeneity of Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) results and proposes taxonomies for understanding heterogeneity in research and reporting practices. His research has implications for psychological research, health assessment, education, and clinical psychology, with a focus on improving the consistency, stability, and applicability of psychometric tools and methods.
